title: DC nodal solver, piecewise-linear devices

implements.text: DC steady state of resistive networks by nodal analysis with partial-pivot Gaussian elimination
LED, diode and NPN as off / on / saturated junction states, re-solved until the states agree (at most 40 rounds)
Rails as a voltage behind 0.5 ohm; output pins as a voltage behind 25 ohm
PWM solved per duty slice and time-averaged
DC motor as a conductance from the part's steady-state curve, up to 6 passes

mocked.text: Regulators, dropout, current limit and brown-out are rules in the power tree, not part of the solve

unsupported.text: Capacitors and inductors; no transient analysis
PNP, MOSFET, op-amp, Zener, regulators as devices
Unit-to-unit variation: identical LEDs share the same forward voltage, so parallel LEDs split current evenly

parameterSources.note: typical AVR pin figure; applied to every board; no citation in bench-solve.js:10

validation.flavour: realistic (author-chosen exponential LED, diode, generic BJT cards)

errorMetrics.name: worst node or branch error vs matched ngspice

operatingRange.evidence: largest circuit in tests/fixtures/fault-corpus/ (clean/ and broken/) has 14 nodes

knownFailureCases: Exits after 40 junction rounds or 6 motor passes without a flag (bench-solve.js:213, 264)
Pin resistance 25 ohm on 3.3 V boards
1N4007 Shockley parameters in the part file are ignored (diode-1n4007.js:31)
Floating subcircuits solve to 0 V without a warning

performance.label: MEASURED
